capabilities.description: Register an existing tmux model server (started manually or outside the cookbook flow) into Cookbook tracking, AND add it as a chat endpoint. Use when the user (or you) launched something via ssh+tmux and now want it visible in the UI / stoppable via stop_served_model / usable in the model picker. Verifies the tmux session + port respond before adding.
capabilities.name: adopt_served_model

add_endpoint.description: Also register as a chat endpoint (default true)

host.description: Remote host in user@host form (e.g. 'user@192.0.2.10'). Omit for localhost.

name.description: Optional display name (defaults to model basename)

port.description: Port the server is listening on (default 8000)

capabilities.description: Call a registered API integration (RSS reader, git forge, bookmark manager, smart home, etc.). Check the system context for available integrations and their endpoints.
capabilities.name: api_call

capabilities.description: Generic loopback to allowed internal Odysseus endpoints. Use this when there's no named tool for what the user wants. Hits the same routes the UI buttons hit (cookbook, gallery, library/documents, memory, notes, calendar, tasks, settings, themes, research, compare, etc.). action='endpoints' returns the OpenAPI surface (use `filter` to narrow). action='call' (default) takes method+path+body. Sensitive auth/user/admin/shell paths and host-control Cookbook mutation routes are blocked for safety. Do not use for shell commands; use named command tooling instead. Do not use for package installs, engine rebuilds, PID signalling, or email account discovery; use list_email_accounts for email accounts because /api/email/accounts is owner-filtered in tool context.
capabilities.name: app_api

action.description: 'call' to hit an endpoint, 'endpoints' to list what's available

filter.description: For action=endpoints: substring to filter paths/summaries (e.g. 'cookbook', 'gallery')

query.description: Querystring params as a key-value object

capabilities.description: Apply a multi-file source-code patch to disk. Use for real project files in the workspace when several edits belong together. Patch must use *** Begin Patch / *** End Patch with Add File, Update File, or Delete File sections. Prefer this over bash redirects/heredocs/sed.
capabilities.name: apply_patch

patch_text.description: Patch text beginning with *** Begin Patch and ending with *** End Patch

capabilities.description: Archive one email by UID. For multiple messages, use bulk_email instead. Always pass account when the email came from a named account such as Gmail.
capabilities.name: archive_email

capabilities.description: Ask a more capable AI model for help when stuck on a difficult problem. The teacher provides guidance that can be saved as a learned skill.
capabilities.name: ask_teacher

model.description: Teacher model name (e.g. 'claude-sonnet-4') or 'auto' for configured default

problem.description: Describe the problem or question you need help with

capabilities.description: Ask the user a multiple-choice question to get a decision or clarification when the task is genuinely ambiguous and the answer changes what you do next (e.g. pick between approaches, confirm an assumption, choose a target). The user sees clickable option buttons; calling this ENDS your turn and their selection arrives as your next message. Prefer sensible defaults over asking — only ask when you truly cannot proceed well without the user's input. Do NOT use it to confirm irreversible/destructive actions that have a dedicated confirmation flow.
capabilities.name: ask_user

multi.description: Set true ONLY when the question explicitly allows choosing more than one option. Otherwise omit it or set false. Default false.

options.description: 2-6 choices. Each is an object with a short `label` and an optional `description` explaining the trade-off.

description.description: Optional one-line explanation of this choice.

label.description: Concise choice text the user clicks (1-5 words).

question.description: The question to ask. Be specific and self-contained.

capabilities.description: Run a shell command (full access). Prefer a dedicated tool whenever one fits the job (reading, writing, editing, searching, or listing files); use bash only for what no dedicated tool covers (installs, git, builds, running programs, system info). Do NOT create or edit files via bash redirects/heredocs/sed -- use the dedicated file tools.
capabilities.name: bash

capabilities.description: Perform one action on many emails at once. Use this for 'delete all those', 'archive these', 'mark all read', or any bulk operation after list_emails. Always pass account when the listed emails came from a named account such as Gmail.
capabilities.name: bulk_email

account.description: Account name/email/id from list_email_accounts, e.g. Gmail or user@example.com

all_unread.description: Operate on all unread messages in folder instead of explicit UIDs

permanent.description: For delete: hard-delete instead of moving to Trash

uids.description: UIDs from the latest list_emails result

capabilities.description: Cancel an in-progress model download by killing its tmux session. Use list_downloads first to get the session_id.
capabilities.name: cancel_download

capabilities.description: Send a message to another AI model and get its response. Use for getting a second opinion, delegating subtasks, or AI-to-AI communication.
capabilities.name: chat_with_model

message.description: The message to send to the model

capabilities.description: Create a new document in the editor panel. Use this when the user asks to write, create, build, make, or generate code, scripts, programs, games, apps, or any long-form or structured content that is more than a short paragraph, AND there is no already-open document/email draft that the request refers to. If an email compose draft is open, edit that draft instead of creating another document. NEVER put large generated content directly in chat — use this tool instead.
capabilities.name: create_document

language.description: Programming language or format (e.g. python, javascript, markdown, text)

capabilities.description: Create a new chat for ongoing conversations with a specific model. (The UI calls these 'chats'; 'session' is the internal term.)
capabilities.name: create_session

capabilities.description: Delete one email by UID. For multiple messages, use bulk_email instead. Always pass account when the email came from a named account such as Gmail.
capabilities.name: delete_email

permanent.description: Hard-delete instead of moving to Trash

capabilities.description: Download a HuggingFace model to a server. If `host` is omitted, defaults to the cookbook's currently-selected server (NOT localhost) — call list_cookbook_servers first if you're unsure where it should go.
capabilities.name: download_model

host.description: Target server — use the friendly NAME from list_cookbook_servers (e.g. 'gpu-box', 'workstation') or a raw user@host. Omit to use the cookbook's selected default server.

local.description: Force download to THIS machine (localhost) instead of the default remote server.

capabilities.description: Edit a document OPEN IN THE EDITOR PANEL (created via create_document) — NOT a file on disk. For files on disk (home folder, project files, anything with a path like ~/x.txt or /path/to/file) use edit_file instead. Targeted find-and-replace with multiple FIND/REPLACE pairs per call; use for any edit smaller than a full rewrite. Do NOT send the whole file back via update_document for small edits.
capabilities.name: edit_document

edits.description: List of find/replace edits (first match only per edit)

find.description: Exact text to find in the document

capabilities.description: Edit a file ON DISK by exact string replacement (home folder, project files, any real path like ~/sweden.txt or /path/to/file). This is the right tool for files on disk — NOT edit_document (that's for editor-panel documents). PREFER this over bash (sed/echo) — it shows a diff. old_string must match the file exactly and be unique (or set replace_all). Use write_file to create a new file.
capabilities.name: edit_file

old_string.description: Exact text to replace (must match the file, including indentation)

replace_all.description: Replace all occurrences instead of requiring a unique match

capabilities.description: Edit a gallery image: upscale, remove background, inpaint, or harmonize.
capabilities.name: edit_image

prompt.description: For inpaint: what to fill the masked area with

capabilities.description: Return the absolute path of the active workspace folder the user is working in. File tools are confined to it; the shell starts there but is not sandboxed. Call this first when the user refers to 'the project'/'the code'/'this folder' without a path, instead of asking them. Takes no arguments.
capabilities.name: get_workspace

capabilities.description: Find files by glob pattern (recursive), newest first. e.g. '**/*.py'. PREFER this over `bash find/ls` for locating files — confined to the allowed roots.
capabilities.name: glob

path.description: Base directory (optional; defaults to the project root)

capabilities.description: Search file contents for a regular expression across a directory tree (uses ripgrep when available, respecting .gitignore). Returns file:line:match. PREFER this over `bash grep/rg` for code search — confined to the allowed roots, structured output.
capabilities.name: grep

glob.description: Only search files matching this glob, e.g. '*.py' (optional)

path.description: Directory or file to search (optional; defaults to the project root)

capabilities.description: List models already cached on disk locally or on a remote server. `host` accepts friendly Cookbook server names from list_cookbook_servers (for example workstation) or raw user@host. Also reports completed Cookbook download tasks when the filesystem cache scan cannot locate the HF cache path.
capabilities.name: list_cached_models

host.description: Friendly Cookbook server name (e.g. 'workstation', 'gpu-box') or raw remote host (e.g. 'user@gpu-box'). Omit for local.

model_dir.description: Comma-separated additional model directories to scan beyond ~/.cache/huggingface/hub

capabilities.description: List the cookbook's configured servers (remote GPU boxes + local) and the current default host. Call this before download_model/serve_model when the user didn't specify a host, so models go to the right machine (where the GPUs and model cache are) instead of localhost. If multiple servers and intent is ambiguous, show them and ask the user which.
capabilities.name: list_cookbook_servers

capabilities.description: List in-progress model downloads in the Cookbook. Shows each download's model name, phase, percent (if available), session ID, and remote host.
capabilities.name: list_downloads

capabilities.description: List configured email accounts. Use this before checking mail when the user names a mailbox/account such as Gmail, work, or a custom domain, then pass the returned account name/email/id to the other email tools.
capabilities.name: list_email_accounts

capabilities.description: List emails from an account/folder, newest first. Returns subject, sender, date, UID, and account for each email. Use list_email_accounts first when the user mentions Gmail/work/a custom mailbox. For last/latest/newest email requests, use max_results=1 and unread_only=false.
capabilities.name: list_emails

account.description: Optional account name/email/id from list_email_accounts, e.g. Gmail or user@example.com

unread_only.description: Only show unread emails. Default false; set true only when the user asks for unread emails.

unresponded_only.description: Only show unanswered emails. Default false.

capabilities.description: List all available AI models across configured endpoints. Optionally filter by keyword.
capabilities.name: list_models

capabilities.description: List saved Cookbook serve presets. Each preset is a launch template (name, model, host, port, tmux cmd) the user previously saved from the UI. Call this BEFORE raw serve_model when the user asks to launch a model by name manually.
capabilities.name: list_serve_presets

capabilities.description: List currently running model servers with status, model name, port, throughput, and structured Cookbook diagnoses. If a serve failed, this includes recent logs plus retry suggestions/adjusted commands the agent can use with serve_model.
capabilities.name: list_served_models

capabilities.description: List the user's chats (the UI calls them 'chats') as clickable markdown links. Use this to enumerate chats before opening, renaming, archiving, or deleting them. When replying to the user, preserve the returned [title](#session-id) links; do not strip them into plain text. Optionally filter by keyword.
capabilities.name: list_sessions

filter.description: Optional keyword to filter chats by name

capabilities.description: List the entries of a directory (folders first, then files with sizes). PREFER this over `bash ls` — confined to the allowed roots.
capabilities.name: ls

path.description: Directory to list (optional; defaults to the project root)

capabilities.description: Inspect and control detached background `bash` jobs (started with the `#!bg` marker). action='list' shows this chat's jobs with id/status/age/command; action='output' returns a job's captured output so far (use for a still-running job, or to re-read a finished one); action='kill' terminates a runaway job's process tree instead of waiting out its max-runtime. output and kill need job_id from list.
capabilities.name: manage_bg_jobs

job_id.description: Background job id (required for output/kill; from action='list')

capabilities.description: Manage calendar events: list events in a date range, create, update, delete. Each event can carry a tag/category (event_type) and importance level. Resolve relative dates like today/tomorrow against the 'Current date and time' system context, then pass ISO 8601 datetimes in the user's local wall time; for all-day events set all_day=true and pass YYYY-MM-DD. For event reminders/alarms, pass reminder_minutes; the tool creates the Odysseus note reminder, so do not also call manage_notes for the same reminder. Do not set rrule for single-occurrence requests such as 'next Wednesday only'; use rrule only when the user explicitly wants recurrence.
capabilities.name: manage_calendar

all_day.description: Whether this is an all-day event

calendar.description: Filter list_events by calendar name or href

calendar_href.description: Specific calendar URL (optional; defaults to first calendar)

dtend.description: End ISO datetime; defaults to +1h (or +1 day for all_day)

dtstart.description: Start ISO datetime, or YYYY-MM-DD if all_day

end.description: list_events range end (ISO datetime). Use this for month/week requests after resolving the date range; defaults to +14 days only when no range is requested. Prefer end; backend also accepts end_time, end_date, range_end, to, dtend, until.

event_type.description: Tag / category for the event. Common values: work, personal, health, travel, meal, social, admin, other. Aliases accepted: tag, category, type.

reminder_minutes.description: For create_event: create an Odysseus reminder this many minutes before the event, e.g. 5 for 'reminder 5 min before'.

rrule.description: Recurrence rule in iCalendar RRULE format, e.g. 'FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO' for weekly on Monday. Use with create_event or update_event. For update_event, pass an explicit empty string to remove recurrence and make the event single-occurrence.

start.description: list_events range start (ISO datetime). Use this for month/week requests after resolving the date range; do not pass a loose query string. Prefer start; backend also accepts start_time, start_date, range_start, from, dtstart, since.

capabilities.description: Create, update, delete, or list the user's CardDAV contacts. Use to save a new contact, update an existing one (email/phone/address), or remove one. Add does not require email: name + phone or name + address is valid. For update/delete you need the contact's uid — call action='list' first to find it. Writes go through the same dedupe + validation as the Contacts UI.
capabilities.name: manage_contact

action.description: list = show all contacts (with uids); add = create; update = edit by uid; delete = remove by uid.

address.description: Postal/mailing address as a single human-readable string.

email.description: Single email address (convenience for add, or the primary email for update). Optional when phone or address is provided.

emails.description: Full list of email addresses (first is primary).

phones.description: Full list of phone numbers. Valid for add/update.

uid.description: Contact UID (required for update/delete; get it from action=list).

capabilities.description: Manage documents: list all documents (with optional search/language filter), delete documents, or run tidy cleanup.
capabilities.name: manage_documents

capabilities.description: Manage model API endpoints: list configured endpoints, add new ones, delete, enable or disable them.
capabilities.name: manage_endpoints

base_url.description: API base URL e.g. https://api.openai.com/v1 (for add)

capabilities.description: Manage MCP (Model Context Protocol) tool servers: list servers and their tools, add new servers, delete, enable/disable, reconnect, or list all available tools.
capabilities.name: manage_mcp

command.description: Command to run e.g. npx (for add)

capabilities.description: Manage the user's memory system: list, add, edit, delete, or search memories. Memories persist across sessions.
capabilities.name: manage_memory

text.description: Memory text (for add/edit) or search query (for search)

capabilities.description: Manage notes and checklists (Google Keep-style): list, view, add, update, delete, toggle_item. Use list/search to find candidate notes, then view with the note id when you need the full body. IMPORTANT: For to-do lists / checklists, set note_type='checklist' and pass the items as the `checklist_items` array — do NOT serialize them into `content` as plain text. For freeform notes, use note_type='note' and put the body in `content`. `due_date` accepts natural language like 'tomorrow at 9am' (parsed in the user's timezone) and fires a notification — do not also create a calendar event for the same reminder.
capabilities.name: manage_notes

archived.description: For update: archive/unarchive. For list: show archived notes when true.

checklist_items.description: Checklist items for note_type='checklist'. Each item is {text, done}. REQUIRED for checklists — leaving this empty produces a blank note.

done.description: Whether the item is checked off

content.description: Freeform body text. Use this for note_type='note'. Do NOT use this for checklists — pass `checklist_items` instead.

due_date.description: Reminder time. Accepts natural language ('tomorrow at 9am', '11pm today') or ISO 8601. Fires a notification at that time.

id.description: Note id (for update/delete/toggle_item); 8-char prefix is fine

label.description: Optional category label (also used as a list filter)

note_type.description: 'note' = freeform text in `content`. 'checklist' = structured to-do items in `checklist_items`. Defaults to 'checklist' if checklist_items is supplied, else 'note'.

pinned.description: Pin the note to the top

capabilities.description: Manage a chat: rename, archive, unarchive, delete, mark important, truncate history, or fork it. (The UI calls these 'chats'; 'session' is the internal term.) For destructive actions like delete, call list_sessions first and pass the exact id returned there; never invent ids.
capabilities.name: manage_session

session_id.description: Exact target chat id from list_sessions, or 'current' for the active chat where supported

capabilities.description: Manage user preferences and settings. Use `disable_tool`/`enable_tool`/`list_tools` to turn individual tools on or off globally (e.g. shell, search, browser, documents, memory, skills, images, tasks, notes, calendar, email). Use list/get/set/delete for free-form preferences.
capabilities.name: manage_settings

tool.description: Tool name to disable/enable (for disable_tool/enable_tool). Accepts aliases: shell, search, browser, documents, memory, skills, images, tasks, notes, calendar, email — or a raw tool name like 'bash' or 'web_search'.

value.description: Setting value (for set) — can be string, number, boolean, or object

capabilities.description: Read or modify the user's skill library. Skills are SKILL.md files (YAML frontmatter + structured body: When to Use / Procedure / Pitfalls / Verification) and follow a draft → published lifecycle. Use progressive disclosure: 'list' to see what exists, 'view' to load full content for a single skill, 'view_ref' for sub-files. Use 'patch' for surgical text edits and 'edit' for full rewrites. 'publish' once you've verified the procedure works. For add, always provide an explicit name slug and only tell the user the exact name returned by the tool.
capabilities.name: manage_skills

action.description: list = name+description summary; view = full SKILL.md; view_ref = sub-file under the skill dir; add = create; edit = full rewrite (content); patch = old_string→new_string; publish = flip status; delete; search = relevance match on published skills.

description.description: One-line summary surfaced in the skills index (for add).

fallback_for_toolsets.description: Hide when these toolsets are active (for add).

name.description: Slug/name of the skill. Required for add/view/view_ref/edit/patch/publish/delete. For add, choose the exact kebab-case name the user should see and report only the returned name.

old_string.description: Exact substring to replace (for patch). Must appear exactly once.

path.description: Sub-path under the skill directory for view_ref (e.g. 'references/example.md').

requires_toolsets.description: Hide unless these toolsets are active (for add).

verification.description: How to confirm the procedure succeeded (for add).

when_to_use.description: Trigger conditions in plain English (for add).

capabilities.description: Manage scheduled/automated tasks: list, create, edit, delete, pause, resume, or run tasks. Use this for ANY recurring/scheduled request ('every morning…', 'each day at 7:30', 'daily summarize…') — create a task rather than doing it once. Task types: llm (AI runs a prompt), research (runs the deep-research pipeline on a question), or action (built-in automation). Triggers can be time-based or event-based.
capabilities.name: manage_tasks

output_target.description: Where results go. Defaults to 'session' (results land in a dedicated chat session the user reads) — this is the right choice for 'summarize for me' / 'send to me'. Do NOT go hunting for the user's email address; only use an email MCP tool name here if the user explicitly asked to be emailed AND an address is already known.

prompt.description: The instruction (for task_type=llm) or the research question (for task_type=research). Required for both.

scheduled_day.description: Day of week 0=Mon (weekly) or day of month (monthly)

scheduled_time.description: HH:MM in UTC (for schedule triggers). Convert the user's stated local time using the UTC offset given in the 'Current date and time' context.

task_type.description: llm = AI runs your prompt; research = runs the deep-research pipeline on the prompt as a question; action = direct built-in function

capabilities.description: Manage API access tokens: list existing tokens, create new ones, or delete them.
capabilities.name: manage_tokens

capabilities.description: Manage webhooks: list, add, delete, enable or disable webhook endpoints.
capabilities.name: manage_webhooks

capabilities.description: Mark one email as read or unread by UID. For multiple messages, use bulk_email instead. Always pass account when the email came from a named account such as Gmail.
capabilities.name: mark_email_read

read.description: True marks read; false marks unread

capabilities.description: Run a multi-step AI pipeline where each model's output feeds the next. Example: Draft -> Critique -> Revise.
capabilities.name: pipeline

capabilities.description: Execute Python code to compute a result or test something. Prefer a dedicated tool whenever one fits the job (reading, writing, or searching files); use python only for computation, data processing, or scripting no dedicated tool covers.
capabilities.name: python

capabilities.description: Read the full content of a specific email by UID.
capabilities.name: read_email

account.description: Optional account name/email/id from list_email_accounts, especially when the UID came from a non-default mailbox

capabilities.description: Read a file from disk. Optionally read a line range with offset/limit for large files.
capabilities.name: read_file

limit.description: Max number of lines to read from offset (optional)

capabilities.description: SEND a reply email immediately by UID. Do not use this when the user asks to write/draft/open/start a reply; use ui_control action=open_email_reply with body instead so the user can review. Only use when the user explicitly says to send now. Use the exact UID from the latest read_email/list_emails result; never invent UID 1. Automatically threads with In-Reply-To/References headers.
capabilities.name: reply_to_email

account.description: Optional account name/email/id from list_email_accounts, especially when the UID came from a non-default mailbox

uid.description: Exact UID of the email to reply to from list_emails/read_email; never invent UID 1

capabilities.description: Look up a contact by name. Searches CardDAV address book and sent email history. Returns email addresses (when available) or phone numbers. Use when the user says 'message [name]', 'email [name]', or asks for someone's contact details.
capabilities.name: resolve_contact

capabilities.description: Scan recent email headers for likely spam/newsletter unsubscribe candidates. Does not unsubscribe anything. Review candidates with the user before acting; mailto methods can be executed with unsubscribe_email, web URL methods require browser/web tools after approval.
capabilities.name: scan_email_unsubscribes

max_scan.description: How many newest emails to inspect (default: 150)

capabilities.description: Search the user's past session transcripts by keyword. Use when the user asks about previous chats, past conversations, or when direct transcript evidence is better than persistent memory. Returns matching sessions with clickable links and nearby context.
capabilities.name: search_chats

query.description: Search keyword(s) to find in past conversations

capabilities.description: Search HuggingFace for models matching a query. Returns a ranked list of repo IDs, sizes (when available), and download counts. Use this when the user wants to find a model to download.
capabilities.name: search_hf_models

capabilities.description: Send a new email. Use resolve_contact first if you only have a name and need to find the email address. If multiple accounts exist, pass account from list_email_accounts.
capabilities.name: send_email

account.description: Optional account name/email/id from list_email_accounts, e.g. Gmail or user@example.com

capabilities.description: Send a new message to an existing live chat and get that chat model's response. Do not use this to retrieve, read, summarize, or inspect old chats; use search_chats or list_sessions for past chat evidence.
capabilities.name: send_to_session

session_id.description: The id of the chat to send the message to

capabilities.description: Start serving a model with vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, MLX Image, or Diffusers. If `host` is omitted, defaults to the cookbook's selected server (not localhost). For MLX image models on Apple Silicon use `python3 scripts/mlx_image_server.py --model <repo> --port 8100`; for non-MLX image/inpainting/diffusion models use `python3 scripts/diffusion_server.py --model <repo> --port 8100`. Never serve image models with `mlx_lm.server`; that is only for text/chat MLX models. After launching, call list_served_models to check readiness/errors; if it reports a diagnosis with retry suggestions, retry via serve_model using the suggested adjusted cmd.
capabilities.name: serve_model

cmd.description: Full serve command (e.g. 'vllm serve <repo> --port 8000 --tp 2', 'python3 -m sglang.launch_server --model-path <repo> --port 30000', for MLX image models: 'python3 scripts/mlx_image_server.py --model <repo> --port 8100', or for non-MLX image models: 'python3 scripts/diffusion_server.py --model <repo> --port 8100')

host.description: Target server — friendly NAME from list_cookbook_servers (e.g. 'gpu-box', 'workstation') or raw user@host. Omit to use the cookbook's selected default.

local.description: Force serve on THIS machine instead of the default remote server.

capabilities.description: Launch a saved Cookbook serve preset by name. Reuses the exact tmux command + host the user saved before. This is the preferred way to start a known model (SD3.5, vLLM presets, etc.) — don't fabricate launch commands when a preset exists.
capabilities.name: serve_preset

name.description: Preset name (exact or case-insensitive substring of one returned by list_serve_presets)

capabilities.description: Stop a running model server.
capabilities.name: stop_served_model

session_id.description: Tmux session ID of the server to stop

capabilities.description: Suggest improvements to the active document WITHOUT editing it. Creates inline comment bubbles the user can accept or reject. Use when the user asks for suggestions, review, improvements, or feedback.
capabilities.name: suggest_document

suggestions.description: List of suggested changes with reasons

find.description: Exact text in the document to suggest changing

reason.description: Brief explanation of why this change helps

capabilities.description: Read the last N lines of a cookbook serve/download task's tmux pane. Use ONLY in this exact sequence: (1) the user asked to serve a model, (2) you launched it via serve_model, (3) list_served_models reports the NEW task as crashed/error, (4) call tail_serve_output on the new sessionId to find the root cause, (5) call serve_model again with adjusted flags. DO NOT call this on old stopped/completed download tasks — they are historical and won't tell you anything about the current attempt. DO NOT investigate past failures before launching; the environment may have changed since.
capabilities.name: tail_serve_output

tail.description: How many lines of pane scrollback to fetch (default 300, max 4000). Bump this if the error in the visible tail references an earlier line ('see root cause above').

capabilities.description: Create and maintain a structured task list for the current coding session. Use during multi-step implementation/debug/refactor work and keep statuses current.
capabilities.name: todowrite

todos.description: Current task list. Only one item should be in_progress.

capabilities.description: Start a deep research task on a topic. Returns a task ID for tracking.
capabilities.name: trigger_research

capabilities.description: Control the user interface. Actions: toggle (turn tools on/off), open_panel (open a modal: documents/library, gallery, email, sessions, notes, memories/brain, skills, settings, cookbook), open_email_reply (open an email reply draft document; DOES NOT send. For 'write/draft a reply saying X', include body with the drafted reply), set_mode, switch_model, set_theme (built-in presets: dark, light, midnight, paper, cyberpunk, retrowave, forest, ocean, ume, copper, terminal, organs, lavender, gpt, claude, cute), create_theme (CREATE any custom theme with a name + colors object — pick distinctive, evocative hex colors that match the requested aesthetic, NOT generic defaults. The theme auto-applies after creation). When a user asks for ANY theme not in the built-in preset list, ALWAYS use create_theme.
capabilities.name: ui_control

action.description: The UI action. Use set_theme for presets, create_theme to build a custom theme with any hex colors

body.description: For open_email_reply: reply body to pre-fill. Required whenever the user told you what the reply should say. Opens a draft, does not send.

accent.description: Accent color for buttons, brand, highlights (hex)

mode.description: Reply draft mode for open_email_reply: reply, reply-all, or ai-reply

name.description: For toggle: web, bash, research, incognito, document_editor (aliases: shell, search, deepresearch, documents). For open_panel: documents, gallery, email, sessions, notes, brain/memories, skills, settings, cookbook. For open_email_reply: email UID. For set_theme: a preset theme name. For create_theme: the custom theme name.

value.description: Value: on/off for toggle, agent/chat for set_mode, model name for switch_model, theme name for set_theme, or folder for open_email_reply

capabilities.description: Execute one approved unsubscribe action for an email UID. Safe mailto List-Unsubscribe methods are sent/staged. Web URL methods return a requires-browser instruction and exact URL; use browser/web tools only after user approval.
capabilities.name: unsubscribe_email

allow_web.description: Return browser/web instructions when selected method is URL

capabilities.description: Replace the ENTIRE active document. ONLY use for genuine full rewrites (>50% of lines changed). For any smaller change, use edit_document — echoing back the whole file for small edits is wasteful.
capabilities.name: update_document

capabilities.description: Write back to the ACTIVE PLAN: mark steps done or revise them. Use this while executing an approved plan — after you finish a step, call update_plan with the full checklist and that step marked `- [x]`; when the user asks to change the plan, call it with the revised checklist. The user's docked plan window updates live. Pass the COMPLETE checklist every time (not a diff). No effect if there is no active plan.
capabilities.name: update_plan

plan.description: The full updated plan as a GitHub-style markdown checklist — one step per line, `- [ ]` for pending and `- [x]` for done. Always send the whole list.

capabilities.description: Fetch and read the text content of a specific URL the user names (e.g. 'check example.com', 'what's on this page <url>'). Use when you already have a concrete URL/domain. NOT for open-ended searches (use web_search) or 'research X' jobs (use trigger_research). Downloads are size-budgeted; a '[partial content: ...]' notice in the result means the body was cut short and you can re-call with full=true for the rest.
capabilities.name: web_fetch

full.description: Raise the download budget to the hard cap for large pages/files. Use only after a result reported partial content.

url.description: The URL or domain to fetch (http/https; a bare domain like example.com is fine)

capabilities.description: Quick single web lookup for a fact or current event mid-task. NOT for 'research X' / 'do research on X' — those are deep-research jobs; use trigger_research instead.
capabilities.name: web_search

time_filter.description: Optional freshness filter for news/latest/today queries

capabilities.description: Write/save a file to disk
capabilities.name: write_file

extensions.digest_formula: interplane Catalog.computed_digest: sha256 over JCS of sorted [name, sha256(JCS(parameters))] pairs (recomputed 2026-10-04; the original extraction used an ad-hoc formula)
